messages.subject: Re: Difficulty graphing with nested data
parts:
Hi:

Dodging points, lines and error bars gets rather messy; I'd suggest you consider faceting to ease the computational and visual load. Here are a couple of alternatives; I renamed your data frame dat to avoid potential conflicts with the data() function.

dat <- read.csv("Example_Data.csv", header = TRUE)
library("ggplot2")

ggplot(dat, aes(x = Treatment, y = Mean, colour = Location, shape = Treatment)) +
   theme_bw() +
   geom_point() +
   geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = Mean - ci, ymax = Mean + ci), colour = "black",
                    width = 0.1) +
   geom_line(aes(group = Location)) +
   labs(x = "Treatment", y = "Mean Time (Hours)", colour = "Location",
        title = "Effect of treatment \nin different populations") +
   theme(panel.grid = element_blank()) +
   facet_wrap(~ Generation, nrow = 1)

ggplot(dat, aes(x = Location, y = Mean, colour = Treatment, shape = Treatment)) +
   theme_bw() +
   geom_point() +
   geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = Mean - ci, ymax = Mean + ci), colour = "black",
                    width = 0.1) +
   geom_line(aes(group = Treatment)) +
   labs(x = "Location", y = "Mean Time (Hours)", colour = "Treatment",
        title = "Effect of treatment \nin different populations") +
   theme(panel.grid = element_blank()) +
   coord_flip() +
   facet_wrap(~ Generation, ncol = 1)

HTH,
Dennis

I have a data set organized like the data in the attached Example_Data.csv file.  I am interested in producing a graph of the data in which points are connected by lines, and each point has it's standard error plotted around it, and the populations are in different colors while the different treatments

Code I have been using is below, with comments on what the problem is that I am having with which command.
_________

data <- read.csv("Example_data.csv")

attach(data)

library(ggplot2)


pd <- position_dodge(0.1)

ggplot(data, mapping = aes(x=Generation, y=Mean, group = Treatment , colour = Location, shape = Treatment))+

geom_errorbar(aes(ymin=Mean-ci, ymax=Mean + ci), colour = "black",width = 0.1, position = pd)+

##geom_line()+   ##Cannot get lines to connect the points properly

geom_point(position = pd, size = 2)+

xlab("Generation")+

ylab("Mean Time (Hours)")+

scale_colour_hue(name = "Location")+

ggtitle("Effect of treatment \nin different populations")+

theme_bw()

I agree with Dennis, consider faceting. But if not, something like
this should work (I also renamed 'data'):

p <- ggplot(d,aes(Generation,Mean,color=Location,shape=Treatment))
p+geom_line(aes(group=paste(Location,Treatment)))+geom_point()+geom_errorbar(aes(ymin=Mean-ci,ymax=Mean+ci))

Ben
